title: Localization of shifted derived Hom from a bounded-below compact source
statement:
Let $\mathcal S$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $A$ be a commutative ring, $t\in A$, and $R$ a sheaf of commutative $A$-algebras. Use module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $R_t=R[1/t]$, the sheafified section localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], and $F:D(R)\to D(R_t)$ for the functor induced termwise by exact scalar localization $M\mapsto R_t\otimes_R M$, with sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the exact-functor derived construction [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Fix $K\in D(R)$ with the following property: for every countable family $(L_n)$ with a common cohomological lower bound and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map $\bigoplus_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L_n[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,(\bigoplus_nL_n)[q])$ is an isomorphism. For every bounded-below $L\in D(R)$ and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the actual scalar-extension map induces an isomorphism of $A[1/t]$-modules
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L[q])[1/t]\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_t)}(FK,FL[q]),\qquad u/t^n\longmapsto t^{-n}F(u).$$
Localization of the Hom module has the fraction relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. These isomorphisms are natural in $K,L$, commute with shifts, and respect identity maps and composition whenever the displayed hypotheses hold for the objects involved. No constructibility, scheme, or essential-surjectivity assertion is included.

proof.text: Sectionwise localization is flat. Evaluation detects finite limits for presheaf tensors, and module sheafification preserves flatness. The regular-module comparison identifies the restricted regular localized ring with this flat sheaf. The natural change-of-rings/tensor comparison identifies E followed by restriction with tensoring by that flat module. Restriction is faithful and detects finite limits. Tensor is additive and the ordinary change-of-rings adjunction makes E a left adjoint, so E preserves finite colimits. This proves scalarLocalization_exact.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2); Stacks algebra.tex 00HT, 00CM, 07JZ; derived.tex 015F, 093W, 094A, 0949

proof.text: Use the normalized ordinary extension/restriction adjunction. Both functors are exact; applying them termwise preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Descend their adjunction along the two localization functors Q using Mathlib Adjunction.localization. Its formula for the unit, followed by cancellation of mapDerivedCategoryFactors and their inverses, gives exactly scalarLocalizationTelescopeDerivedUnit. The ordinary unit section formula is x mapped to the sheafification of 1 tensor x. Coefficient compatibility follows by applying the adjunction to scalar identity maps and by the coefficient localization lift formula. The corresponding compatibility on derived Homs follows first on Q of complexes using its linearity and the factorization natural isomorphism, then on arbitrary objects by essential surjectivity.

proof.text: For bounded-below L apply the normalized underlying scalar-localization telescope. Apply sequence_relative_hom_telescope to the constant sequence L with transition t times identity. The shifted comparison is the continuity hypothesis at q=1. The unshifted comparison follows from its q=0 case by the shift-zero isomorphism and the pointwise direct-sum additive equivalence. Postcompose with the telescope vertex isomorphism and then take the inverse additive adjunction equivalence. Naturality of the unit and the triangle identity show that the class of f at stage n is sent to t^(-n) F(f).

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2); Stacks algebra.tex 00HT, 00CM, 07JZ; derived.tex 015F, 093W, 094A, 0949

proof.text: Identify the module colimit of multiplication by t with localized fractions by localization_away_colimit. The forgetful functor from modules to abelian groups preserves colimits, and the identity natural isomorphism identifies that forgotten sequence with the Hom sequence from the preceding step. Thus the additive equivalence sends f/t^n to t^(-n) F(f). This equivalence is A-linear by coefficient compatibility and fraction induction. Extend scalars to A[1/t] using Mathlib LinearEquiv.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2); Stacks algebra.tex 00HT, 00CM, 07JZ; derived.tex 015F, 093W, 094A, 0949

proof.text: Apply the preceding calculation to L[q], bounded below at b-q. Postcomposition with the canonical F.commShiftIso q gives the required shifted equivalence, with its normalized formula on every fraction. Naturality follows from map_comp and commShiftIso naturality; the identity follows from commShiftIso_zero; composition follows from commShiftIso_add, the shift functor linearity, and t^(-(n+m))=t^(-n)t^(-m); simultaneous shifts follow from map_shiftFunctorComm_hom_app and commShiftIso naturality. These elementary equations prove all clauses of scalarLocalizationHomComparison.
